fixes.explanation: No gifts in this scene, friend. These men walked in with empty sacks and a long list of worries. The text says they “…bowed down before him with their faces to the ground.” (Genesis 42:6) That's the first thing the verse shows them doing, and they came to buy grain from the man in charge.

Judah's a fair guess, friend, since he's a big name in this family. But the text gives this line to Reuben: “Didn’t I tell you not to sin against the boy? But you would not listen.” (Genesis 42:22) I think this is a heavy moment, with years of regret coming out all at once.

Levi is one of the brothers there, but he's not the one speaking. Verse 22 says Reuben responded, “Didn’t I tell you not to sin against the boy?” (Genesis 42:22) I think this one hurts. Reuben is reminding them that he warned them, and they all have to carry what happened.

I'd lean True on this one, baker. The text says, “They did not realize that Joseph understood them, since there was an interpreter between them.” (Genesis 42:23) So they talk freely right in front of him. I think that's a lot to sit through quietly.

A place to live near the ruler sounds nice, but nobody offers a room with a view. The man says, “Then I will give your brother back to you, and you can trade in the land.” (Genesis 42:34) Their brother back and the right to trade. That's the whole deal, friend, and it only comes after the youngest brother shows up.
